subject: Food Science
title: Prion Diseases
description: A micro-lesson that makes Prion Diseases usable.

hook.text: Mad cow disease is caused by a misfolded protein—not a virus, not a bacterium. It can't be killed by cooking or bleach.

buildup.text: Prions are infectious proteins that force normal brain proteins to misfold. The result is always fatal brain degeneration.

discovery.text: The UK's BSE crisis in the 1990s killed 178 people who ate contaminated beef. Over 4 million cattle were culled.

twist.text: Prions resist autoclaving at 134°C, UV light, and chemical disinfection. They're virtually indestructible.

climax.text: Feed bans—stopping the practice of feeding animal remains to cattle—virtually eliminated BSE worldwide.

punchline.text: Not alive, can't be killed, always fatal. Prions break every rule of biology.

quiz.question: What are prions?
options: Misfolded infectious proteins that cause fatal brain disease
